correspondences.rationale: Both denote a hard transmitter-laser defect that compromises or extinguishes the outgoing wavelength.
Both denote a terminal card/module hardware outage that loses traffic and telemetry and masks subordinate alarms.
Both are receiver-local degradations producing errors while the optical route and other wavelengths remain healthy.
Both denote gradual transmit-laser ageing evidenced by rising bias current and predictive of eventual failure.
Both denote a slow receiver-observed erosion of wavelength margin that eventually causes errors or frame loss.
Both denote a physical fibre discontinuity that removes incoming optical and supervisory signals.
Both denote complete amplifier loss of operation with no output light and downstream wavelength impact.
Both denote disconnection of a launch or section-input optical jumper that interrupts downstream light.
Both denote excessive added loss on an upstream fibre span that sharply reduces received optical power.
Both denote amplifier-added optical noise that lowers OSNR despite potentially normal signal power.
Both denote increasing upstream differential group delay that impairs coherent reception.
Both denote router/WSS passband misalignment that clips one channel and degrades quality despite normal level.
Both denote a rapid polarization change capable of outrunning receiver tracking and causing errors.
Both denote connector contamination that adds optical impairment and degrades the received wavelength.
Both are deliberately nonspecific faults anywhere on a relevant active or protected ODU path.
Both denote an amplifier gain deficiency relative to its configured target.
Both denote gradual amplifier-pump ageing, rising drive current, and eventual end-of-life indication.
Both denote wavelength-dependent amplifier gain imbalance that weakens channels near one band edge.
Both denote a hard physical failure of an ODU cross-connect switching fabric.
Both denote an incorrect ODU cross-connect that sends traffic to the wrong destination.
Both denote a hard failure of a customer-facing client or tributary interface.
Both denote failure of one router directional input, blocking all channels from that direction while others continue.
Both denote absence of detectable incoming optical light at a receiver or optical module.
Both denote inability to recover valid OTU framing, including cases where light remains present.
Both denote an equipment-level terminal card/module failure leading to dEQ and loss of framing.
Both denote suppression of subordinate traffic alarms by a module-level hardware alarm.
Both are composite received-light degradation states encompassing power, noise, DGD, filtering, or receiver penalties.
Both denote pre-FEC errors above the receiver's degradation threshold while framing may remain intact.
Both denote polarization changes faster than the coherent receiver can track.
Both denote one-second intervals containing qualifying transmission errors.
Both denote insertion of ODU AIS downstream on every ODU affected by OTU frame loss.
Both denote returning a backward defect indication to the transmitting terminal.
Both denote a transmit laser that has stopped or failed and compromises the outgoing wavelength.
Both denote loss of traffic arriving at the failed local module.
Both denote cessation of telemetry and status reporting from failed equipment.
Both describe the unaffected route and other wavelengths remaining healthy despite a receiver-local fault.
Both denote increasing transmitter-laser bias as the laser ages.
Both denote a gradual reduction in one wavelength's receiver margin.
Both denote below-expected amplifier output power affecting the carried wavelengths.
Both denote a downstream OSNR or noise penalty affecting carried wavelengths.
Both denote zero optical output from a device, potentially despite input light.
Both denote transparent forwarding of an input condition or signal to the output.
Both denote the design in which every hut or shelter terminates the incoming supervisory link and starts a new one.
Both denote confinement of a supervisory-channel outage to the fibre span where it occurs.
Both denote normal measured optical level despite another quality impairment.
Both denote gradual increase of the local amplifier pump-drive indicator during ageing.
Both denote an ageing trend culminating in the pump end-of-life indication.
Both denote a wavelength remaining below target power downstream of optical routing or amplification.
Both denote failure to receive the incoming optical supervisory signal.
Both denote measured amplifier gain deviating by more than 2 dB from its configured target.
Both denote pump drive exceeding 120% of its initial reference value.
Both denote receipt of the wrong ODU identity because the ODU was misrouted.
Both denote unavailability of the customer-facing service.
Both denote protected service configuration with working/primary and protection/standby ODU routes.
Both denote availability of a defect-free alternative route for the protection selector.
Both denote only a brief traffic interruption during protection switching.
Both denote delivery of one ODU to an unintended destination.
Both denote independent switching or steering of each wavelength.
Both denote propagation of a direction-wide ingress impairment onto each independently routed wavelength.
Both denote node or router equalization restoring wavelength power to its target launch level.
Both denote an impairment traversing a network element without being removed.
Both denote degraded signal integrity without requiring total signal loss.
Both denote all traffic from one failed router input being prevented from passing onward.
Both denote traffic on unaffected router directions continuing normally.
Both are measurements of optical power received for an individual wavelength.
Both are telemetry counters of one-second intervals containing errors.
Both measure or estimate per-wavelength optical signal-to-noise ratio.
Both measure the fraction of erroneous bits before forward-error correction.
Both measure differential group delay on the received coherent signal.
Both measure how rapidly the received state of polarization changes.
Both express current transmitter-laser bias as a percentage of its initial commissioning reference.
Both measure aggregate optical power entering an amplifier.
Both measure aggregate optical power leaving an amplifier.
Both express amplifier pump drive as a percentage of its initial reference.
Both indicate whether the incoming optical supervisory link is being received.
Both count seconds during which the customer/client service is unavailable.
Both denote a single-client 400G wavelength transponder with coherent optical and laser-health monitoring.
Both denote the optical amplifier at the transmitting launch end of a wavelength section.
Both denote an in-line optical amplifier deployed at an intermediate hut or shelter.
Both denote the receiving-end pre-amplifier immediately before the next routing or receiving node.
Both digitally cross-connect ODUs between line and customer-facing interfaces.
Both denote a physical customer-facing client service interface.
Both denote an optical routing resource that independently directs wavelengths between line directions.
Both are urgent/critical alarms for absent incoming optical light at a wavelength receiver.
Both indicate loss of recoverable OTU framing.
Both indicate pre-FEC errors above the signal-degradation threshold while framing remains.
Both report that the far end detected a defect in the locally transmitted OTU.
Both are equipment alarms for a local transmit-laser hardware fault.
Both are equipment alarms for a local wavelength card or module hardware failure.
Both indicate transmitter-laser bias exceeding 120% of its initial reference.
Both indicate absent incoming optical light at an optical amplifier; model B combines amplifier and terminal variants.
Both indicate loss of the incoming span supervisory optical channel.
Both indicate an amplifier with no optical output light.
Both indicate amplifier gain deviating by more than 2 dB from target.
Both indicate pump drive above 120% of its initial reference and impending end of life.

Both are urgent alarms for hardware failure of the local ODU switching fabric.
